summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour delivers a profound lecture on divine purpose and predestination by examining the life of Prophet Musa (Moses) from the Quran. He explores how Musa was born during the year of genocide in Egypt, an apparent tragedy that was actually part of Allah's meticulous design for his life. Sh. Ali Mashhour emphasizes that every hardship Musa faced—being hidden in a basket in the Nile, burning his tongue and developing a lisp, fleeing as a fugitive—was precisely orchestrated by Allah to prepare him for his ultimate role as one of the greatest messengers. He illustrates how Musa only understood the purpose behind these trials when Allah spoke to him at Mount Sinai, declaring 'I have meticulously formed you under my direct supervision for my use.' Sh. Ali Mashhour connects this to the broader Islamic principle that the greatest destiny anyone can have is to be chosen as an instrument of Allah's will. He concludes with practical advice: believers should focus on obedience and readiness rather than questioning Allah's plans, trusting that when Allah calls upon them, they will be prepared. The lecture includes community announcements about youth programs and halaqas.
